eyebrow: A PRAYER SERIES ON COMPARING YOUR LIFE TO EVERYONE ELSE'S
coverTitle:
Five Prayers
For Feeling
Left Behind
coverDek: For the engagement post that wrecked your morning, the body you keep measuring against a filter, and the quiet math that says everyone else is ahead — five prayers for finally looking at your own plate again.

points.hook: Everyone else's life looks finished. Mine still looks like a draft.
paragraphs: I scroll through a parade of other people's best five seconds and grade my whole unedited life against it — the promotion I don't have yet, the ring I'm not wearing, the body that doesn't look like that this morning. Paul warned that measuring ourselves by ourselves and comparing ourselves among ourselves was never wise, and I'm starting to believe him, because nobody is actually running the same race I am. Lord, let me close the tab on their story long enough to actually read mine.
points.verseText: For we dare not make ourselves of the number, or compare ourselves with some that commend themselves: but they measuring themselves by themselves, and comparing themselves among themselves, are not wise.

points.hook: I decree: their lane does not cancel mine.
paragraphs: I decree over my life tonight that the grace running someone else's race is not the measuring stick for my own — every man shall prove his own work and find his rejoicing in himself, not in a side-by-side with somebody else's highlight reel! I refuse to let another person's season set the clock on mine. In the name of Jesus, the comparison trap breaks off my mind right now, and I pick my pace back up and run it to win.
points.verseText: But let every man prove his own work, and then shall he have rejoicing in himself alone, and not in another.

points.hook: Notice what your body does the second you see their announcement.
paragraphs: Notice it — the tightening in your chest, the breath you hold without meaning to, the quiet drop in your stomach before your mind has even caught up to what you're feeling. That reaction isn't proof something is wrong with you; it's just old wiring firing on cue. Before you spiral into everything you think you lack, let that tightness be the signal to look up and remember whose child you actually are — fearfully and wonderfully made before anyone else's life ever existed to measure against.
points.verseText: I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made: marvellous are thy works; and that my soul knoweth right well.

points.hook: Somebody in this church measures their whole life against somebody else's highlight reel every single day.
paragraphs: Family, somebody reading this right now has quietly decided they're behind — behind in marriage, behind in ministry, behind in everything — because they keep holding their backstage up against everybody else's stage. We are one body with different parts for a reason; the eye was never built to do the hand's job, and your calling was never built to look like your neighbor's calling. If that's you today, stop apologizing for your own pace.
points.verseText: For as we have many members in one body, and all members have not the same office: so we, being many, are one body in Christ, and every one members one of another.

points.hook: Child, I wasn't comparing you to anyone when I made you.
paragraphs: Child, I knew you before I had anything to compare you to, and I never once held another person's life up next to yours while I was forming you in secret. Every good thing I have for you was written in a book before you had done anything to earn it or lose it to somebody else's pace. Stop reading somebody else's chapter over their shoulder; come and let Me show you the one I'm actually writing for you.
points.verseText: Thou hast possessed my reins: thou hast covered me in my mother's womb... thine eyes did see my substance, yet being unperfect; and in thy book all my members were written, which in continuance were fashioned, when as yet there were none of them.

cta.closingLine: If their highlight reel has been setting the pace for your whole week, you're not alone — come back tomorrow for the next series.
